key_insight: FrozenLGP makes divide-and-conquer QAOA work on dense or highly connected graphs by freezing a minimal set of blocking qubits and preserving their effect as bias terms.
engineering_relevance: This turns graph partitionability from a hard prerequisite into an adaptive preprocessing step for scaling QAOA on near-term quantum hardware.
method: Use max-flow/min-cut to find the minimum set of obstructing vertices when standard partitioning fails.
Classically freeze those vertices' spin assignments instead of forcing an invalid separator.
Fold removed interaction energy into linear Ising bias terms on neighboring active qubits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 100% decomposition coverage up to 10,000 vertices, versus 4.6% for the standard baseline on high-connectivity graphs, with preserved MaxCut quality and improved noise robustness.
watch_item: The approach relies on classical preprocessing and spin freezing, so performance may depend on the quality and cost of repeated min-cut computations and on how freezing choices affect solution optimality.
paper_title: Adaptive Qubit Freezing Enables Robust Graph Partitioning for Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
